articles.title: Sophie Cunningham calls some coaches "soft" and opens another controversial debate
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard has questioned the way modern basketball coaches approach player development
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard has questioned the way modern basketball coaches approach player development
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has sparked another debate about the culture surrounding women's basketball after suggesting that some coaches have become too reluctant to challenge their players.

The Indiana Fever guard made her feelings clear during an episode of her podcast, No Hesitation, alongside NBA trainer Drew Hanlen .

Their discussion focused on whether modern coaching methods are helping athletes reach their full potential or making it harder for them to develop the mental toughness required to succeed.

Cunningham's message was straightforward: she wants coaches to demand more from their players rather than worrying excessively about how criticism might be received.

“Bring back hard coaching,” she said, arguing that the most successful athletes often benefit from coaches who are willing to challenge them when standards begin to slip.

She explained that her own development was shaped by people who recognised her abilities but refused to allow her to become complacent: “That is why all of us pros are where we are, because we had coaches who truly cared about us and loved us and saw our full potential. But with that, they didn’t let us slip. If we weren’t going hard enough, or we weren’t doing that, they were on our a–.

“You can’t always listen to their tone. You have to listen to the message. I do think that coaches are too soft on athletes nowadays. Maybe it’s the parents, maybe it’s the athletes who can’t take it, but then y’all shouldn’t be in the sport because if your coach is on you, that means they see something in you.”

Her comments came after Hanlen discussed his experiences working with female basketball players and suggested that they were not always pushed as aggressively as their male counterparts.

Drew Hanlen believes female players deserve the same demanding approach

Hanlen , who has worked with NBA stars including Jayson Tatum, Bradley Beal and Tyrese Haliburton , believes the coaching industry sometimes underestimates what female athletes can handle.

He recalled working with elite women who were surprised by the intensity of his training sessions: “I used to work with all these top women, and they are like, ‘I have never been pushed this hard.'”

Hanlen explained that his philosophy does not change depending on an athlete's gender.

“You’re still a hooper. I don’t care if you’re a guy or a girl. I’m going to train you to my fullest capabilities,” he said.

He believes some coaches are overly concerned that female athletes might struggle emotionally or physically with demanding instruction. In his view, that approach can prevent players from discovering how much they are capable of achieving.

Hanlen's experience gives the discussion another dimension. After playing college basketball at Belmont, he established Pure Sweat Basketball and developed a reputation for working with professional players and promising young talents.

Cunningham's argument is therefore not simply about being shouted at during practice. Both believe criticism should have a purpose: improving performance, developing confidence and holding players responsible for their decisions.

Caitlin Clark provides an example of accountability

Caitlin Clark 's development offers an interesting example of how demanding coaching can influence a young player's career.

During her high school years, coach Kristin Meyer occasionally benched Clark when she showed frustration towards referees or displayed body language that Meyer believed could negatively affect the team.

Meyer understood Clark's talent but wanted her to recognise that individual reactions could have consequences for the entire group.

The lessons were not always comfortable, but they were intended to prepare Clark for the expectations of higher-level basketball.

Cunningham is currently an unrestricted free agent after Indiana's 2026 playoff elimination, leaving questions about where she will play next season. Her comments also arrive during a wider discussion about how the WNBA continues to develop its players and compete at the highest level.

There is, however, an important distinction between demanding coaching and disrespectful treatment. Holding athletes accountable does not mean humiliating them or ignoring their wellbeing.

Ultimately, Cunningham's argument is that genuine support sometimes requires difficult conversations. Coaches should recognise potential, communicate high expectations and challenge players to improve, rather than avoiding criticism altogether. Whether everyone agrees with her assessment, the debate she has raised is unlikely to disappear.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham breaks her silence after Democrats sweep Congress with a message about America’s future
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard reshared a post urging Americans to focus on personal responsibility
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard reshared a post urging Americans to focus on personal responsibility
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham reacted to Democrats’ sweeping midterm victories with a message about the future of the country : lasting change, she suggested, depends on more than elections and politicians. The Indiana Fever guard reshared an Instagram Story from entrepreneur Andy Frisella on Wednesday, the day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress.

The post was Frisella’s, not a statement written by Cunningham, and it did not mention a political party or candidate. It argued that people place too much faith in elections to change their lives and not enough in their ability to lead themselves. “Personal excellence is the Ultimate Rebellion,” the post concluded.

Sophie Cunningham’s message focused on personal responsibility

Frisella’s message said that a country’s strength reflects the character, discipline and standards of its people. It also argued that changing political leaders or passing new laws cannot, by itself, address deeper problems in society. Sophie reshared the post without adding a separate comment.

The timing drew attention because Sophie Cunningham has previously been pulled into political conversations over her views on women’s sports.

In an interview with ESPN, she said her political beliefs were “very much in the middle” and that people often make assumptions about them. She also said she wanted to protect girls in sports while insisting that her position did not mean she hated transgender people.

The Indiana Fever guard’s latest post did not explain how she viewed the election results or identify which party she believes has the answers. Instead, the message she chose to share pointed toward individual choices and standards as part of what shapes America’s future.

She shared the message after Democrats won control of Congress, but she didn’t comment directly on the results. Instead, the post focused on a simple idea: change also starts with people and the choices they make.

articles.title: Two Caitlin Clark trading cards make first contract with Indiana Fever look ridiculous
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star's memorabilia attracted extraordinary bids
articles.summary: The WNBA star's memorabilia has attracted extraordinary bids
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark 's arrival in the WNBA transformed the fortunes of the Indiana Fever , but two remarkable auction sales have provided an extraordinary reminder of how little the league initially paid one of its most commercially valuable stars.

When Indiana selected Clark with the first overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft, she signed a four-year rookie contract worth $338,056, a relatively modest agreement considering the attention already surrounding her college basketball career.

Less than two years later, collectors were spending considerably more than that amount on individual pieces of memorabilia bearing her signature, highlighting the enormous demand surrounding the former Iowa standout.

The most striking example came in July 2025, when a rare Clark rookie card sold for $660,000, nearly doubling the entire value of her original Indiana contract.

That transaction followed another historic sale just four months earlier, when a different autographed card fetched $366,000 and established a new benchmark for women's sports memorabilia.

The figures illustrated a remarkable disparity between her initial WNBA salary and the value collectors placed on her memorabilia.

Record-breaking cards reveal extraordinary demand

The first major milestone arrived in March 2025, when Goldin sold a one-of-one 2024 Panini Prizm WNBA Signatures Gold Vinyl card for $366,000.

The collectible featured Clark 's autograph and carried a perfect PSA 10 grade, surpassing the previous women's sports card record of $266,400, established by a Serena Williams rookie card in 2022.

However, that record survived only four months before a 2024 Panini Flawless Platinum Rookie Logowoman Patch card attracted extraordinary interest during the Fanatics Collect July Premier Auction.

The card included Clark 's autograph alongside the handwritten message "769 pts and counting," celebrating the scoring record she established during her debut WNBA campaign.

After entering extended bidding at $336,000, the collectible eventually sold for $660,000, setting another record for a women's sports trading card.

The difference was particularly remarkable given Clark earned just $78,066 from her Indiana contract in 2025, meaning the auction price exceeded her annual playing salary more than eightfold.

Salary finally catches up with WNBA growth

Clark 's extraordinary popularity has been supported by performances that immediately established her among the league's leading players.

During her rookie season, she averaged 19.2 points, 5.7 rebounds and 8.4 assists, helping Indiana reach the playoffs for the first time since 2016.

She also established rookie records with 769 points and 122 three-pointers, while her 337 assists set a new WNBA single-season benchmark.

The Fever experienced a dramatic attendance increase following her arrival, averaging 17,035 spectators per home game as interest in the franchise surged.

That growing commercial momentum coincided with significant changes to the league's financial structure, including a new collective bargaining agreement that substantially increased player compensation.

Under the revised agreement, Clark 's 2026 salary rose to $528,846, compared with the $85,873 originally scheduled under her rookie contract.

The increase represents important progress, but the historic memorabilia sales demonstrate how rapidly Clark 's commercial appeal developed beyond the financial expectations established when she first entered professional basketball.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark shows lots of love to Jack Campbell as he recovers from his horrific injury
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star showed her support for Jack Campbell and his wife after the Lions linebacker shared an encouraging update on his recovery from a serious neck injury.
articles.summary: The WNBA star showed her support for Jack Campbell and his wife after the Lions linebacker shared an encouraging update on his recovery from a serious neck injury.
articles.body:
On Wednesday, Caitlin Clark sent a heartfelt message of support to Jack Campbell and his wife, Megan, after the Detroit Lions linebacker shared his first update since suffering a serious neck injury last Sunday.

The WNBA star reposted Campbell’s message to Lions fans on her Instagram Stories, adding three blue heart emojis and tagging Megan as a show of support for the family.

In his statement, Campbell revealed that he has full movement in his legs, though he continues to work hard to regain mobility in the upper part of his body.

The linebacker also took the opportunity to thank the fans, the Lions organization, and the medical staff who have supported him since the moment of the injury.

Dan Campbell explains how the Lions will honor Jack Campbell

The Detroit Lions defeated the Minnesota Vikings 19-15 on Sunday, but the victory took a back seat following Jack Campbell ’s frightening injury. Now, as the team prepares to face the Miami Dolphins , the linebacker remains a constant source of motivation in the locker room.

Head coach D an Campbell said on Wednesday that the best way to honor his player will be to compete with the same intensity and commitment that Jack always showed on the field.

"I know the only way to really honor Jack, and what he really wants, is to make sure that we're locked in and ready to go. Because otherwise, what just came about, then we're throwing it away, in a sense. I think we owe it to him. We owe it to all of ourselves to make sure we're locked in and we make the most of this," Dan Campbell told reporters.

Jack Campbell suffered the injury while making a tackle in the fourth quarter of the game against Minnesota . After the impact, he remained motionless on the field, prompting medical personnel to rush in, stabilize him, and carefully remove him from the field for specialized care.

articles.standfirst: Reese received a hero’s welcome from the place where her basketball career took off
articles.summary: Reese received a hero’s welcome from the place where her basketball career took off
articles.body:
T he Bayou Barbie is back at LSU. Although Angel Reese did not get to lift the WNBA trophy this season, she was welcomed like a champion when she returned to the college that helped establish her as one of basketball’s biggest names. She made the visit alongside a proud Kim Mulkey, reuniting with the coach who guided her during her time with the Tigers.

Despite the warm reception and the overwhelming support from the crowd, some fans noticed that Reese still appeared a little down . The loss to the Golden State Valkyries was a tough one, especially after a series that felt like it had slipped away from her team. But that did not stop the LSU faithful from celebrating her return and giving her the title of Queen of the South.

A champion in Baton Rouge

Reese's return was well deserved after what she accomplished during her two seasons at LSU. The Tigers posted a 65-8 record during her time with the program, won a national championship and reached the Elite Eight the following year. She averaged 20.9 points and 14.4 rebounds per game in Baton Rouge, establishing herself as one of the most dominant players in college basketball.

She was also honored before the game, walking onto the court alongside Mulkey as the crowd cheered. Her former coach then presented her with a large bouquet of flowers, adding another moment to an emotional homecoming . Reese went on to reach the WNBA Finals after putting together one of the strongest performances of her professional career.

Reese plans to focus on herself during the offseason

Now that her season is over, Reese is preparing to take some time away from her usual commitments. Earlier this week, she announced on Instagram that she would dedicate the offseason to herself, which also means stepping away from podcasting. However, she will continue sharing some of her life through vlogs on YouTube.

After encouraging her followers to subscribe to her channel, Reese revealed that she plans to spend the offseason living in Florida. Her schedule will include resting, working out, quietly developing her personal brand and spending time supporting and being there for her partner.

articles.title: Who is Lorena Torres? The Spanish guru of the Valkyries: the 1 billion team revolutionizing the WNBA
articles.standfirst: Ibiza-born Lorena Torres has revolutionized women's basketball and the WNBA as director of performance and the medical department for the WNBA champion Valkyries
articles.summary: Ibiza-born Lorena Torres has revolutionized women's basketball and the WNBA as director of performance and the medical department for the WNBA champion Valkyries
articles.body:
"This is what happens when you invest in women's sports" . Those were the words spoken by shooting guard Tiffany Hayes in front of the 18,064 people who packed the Balhalla arena after the Golden State Valkyries lifted the WNBA champhionship trophy last Saturday.

They take care of every detail so that the only thing you have to worry about is playing basketball

A historic milestone in American sports, since the franchise was created just two seasons ago by signing players other teams had deemed expendable and now everything these Valkyries touch turns to gold.

Golden State Valkyries: the first $1 billion WNBA franchise

A few months ago, they became the first WNBA franchise to be valued at $1 billion , according to U.S. media. In addition, they have sold out every home game they have played during their two years of existence, filling the Chase Center, renamed Ballhala when they play .

Specifically, the seventh game of the finals against the Atlanta Dream has been the most-watched in WNBA playoff history, drawing more than 3.3 million television viewers. Quite a record in the league's 30-year history.

The Valkyries have Spanish native Lorena Torres as director of performance and the medical department

"They take care of every detail so that the only thing you have to worry about is playing basketball," said the "Most Valuable Player" (MVP) of the finals, Gabby Williams , about the way the franchise works.

The French-American forward delivered an unforgettable performance in the decisive game, scoring 28 points in the second half against the Dream. At the most important moment of the season, the best version of Gabby emerged, and one of the people responsible for that was Spanish Lorena Torres, the director of performance and head of the Valkyries' medical department.

Everyone believed in the strategy. I'm happy to have been able to help Gabby Williams, who is the star, and other members of the team perform at their highest level when they needed to do so

"At the end-of-season interviews, analyzing individually how things had gone, Gabby thanked me because she told me: "the minute management worked out super well for me, I felt good when I needed to feel good,"" the woman from Ibiza explained to EFE.

As an expansion team, you don't have access to superstars because the system is what it is. Teams try to have the "Big 3," and we had to think of a different strategy

Torres is ultimately responsible for making sports-related decisions such as, for example, the duration and intensity of training sessions or the players' recovery processes.

We designed a roster in which we had depth on the bench, and that has allowed us throughout the season to manage the players' minutes on the court

"Everyone believed in the strategy. I am happy to have been able to help this player, who is the star, and others on the team perform at their highest level when they needed to do so," she said.

Lorena Torres: "It's hard for people to understand what we have achieved"

The arrival of these Valkyries, with a collective, team-oriented style of play and without major "superstars" on their roster, has caused a real earthquake in American women's basketball, which usually tends toward a more individualistic game centered on star players.

Natalie Nakase's team, with this collective success, has redefined the league's standard and could be the beginning of a new era.

The sixth and seventh players are key. I told that to the General Manager. I think it is a more European style, different and, this year, it has worked

"It’s complex for people to understand what we have achieved. As an expansion team, you don’t have access to superstars because the system is what it is. Teams try to have the 'Big 3' and we had to think of another strategy. We designed a roster in which we had bench depth and that has allowed us throughout the season to manage the players’ minutes, because we knew that when the bench started playing, they were going to hold the score for us," reflected the Spaniard.

Maybe next season we'll have three superstars and I'll have to manage that context

This has been one of the keys to the success on the court of the San Francisco franchise. Frenchwoman J anelle Salaün has been selected as the "Best Sixth Player" of the season , contributing 12.7 points off the bench.

And this recognition is no coincidence because, as Torres herself acknowledges, following her time with the Spanish national team or NBA franchises such as the Spurs or the Sixers throughout her career.

"The sixth and seventh men are key. I told the General Manager that. I think it's a more European style, different and, this year, it has worked. Maybe next season we will have three superstars and I will have to manage that context," she concluded.

Lorena Torres's R&D in the Valkyries' success in the WNBA

In an interview with EFE, Lorena Torres reviews her career and explains how she turned the challenge of building a franchise from scratch into a historic success.

Just two seasons into the franchise's existence and they have already won the championship. Are they aware of the magnitude of what they have achieved?

It has been very exciting. Yesterday in meetings we were all saying: is this real? Have we done it? We are a bit in "shock." We have gone game by game and we have won; although it was the objective, it still feels like wow!. We have filled the Warriors' arena (NBA) in every game with our own fans. The Warriors' fans and ours are not the same, but sport is entertainment and if you provide it, there is room for everyone. It feels like being in the right place at the right time.

How has this success been experienced from the inside?

With great emotion, great joy. People are not aware of how hard it has been, of how little time we had to win a ring. The game started how we wanted because if Atlanta started hitting threes, then it is very difficult to stop them. In the last 45 seconds of the game I was looking at the floor, I didn't want to see what was happening, but I lifted my head and saw that everyone was there with the confetti, jumping…

When you're given the opportunity to build the performance department from scratch, how do you approach it? How do you manage to win the WNBA championship in just two seasons?

In 2024 this franchise didn’t exist. Last year was a bit about survival; we wanted to make the playoffs. I focused on building a working team, a staff, the processes, what our warm-ups were going to be like… We were building everything, while the coaching staff was focused on winning games.

But in the postseason, when we had time to analyze how the season was going, the General Manager, the coach and I, who are the triangle of women who make all the sporting decisions, decided to come up with a strategy to reach the "playoffs" in our best possible form, with the goal of winning.

My role was to design a strategy so that throughout the entire season we could keep the players as healthy as possible. I was responsible for deciding how to train and how to rest, the duration of the training sessions, the intensity, etc. And having depth on the bench has allowed us all season to manage the players' minutes on the court.

The load-recovery strategy and the constant feedback with the players has helped us a lot in what we have achieved.

Throughout her career, she has been part of many winning teams, such as the Spanish men's national team, the San Antonio Spurs, or the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers, but what is different about this franchise compared to the others she has worked for?

The biggest difference is that I had always gone to places where the system was already in place and you arrived to contribute your experience, your knowledge. Building everything from scratch has been different and very beautiful because I had free rein to do whatever I wanted.

The collaboration has also been different. I had never been in a place where I had so much influence in decision-making, in strategy, in my role. For me, the collaboration and communication between the General Manager, the coach, and the person in charge of performance and health (her) has been unique. It has been spectacular.

As a franchise, in my second year I’ve seen that in this franchise, if they believe in you, they help you tremendously. Having them believe in you, respect you, and support you boosts performance tremendously.

For me personally, working in a women's environment. I have worked for many years in male-dominated environments and it is different. It has been a very healthy environment; we want to have good people, to be part of building such a healthy culture in the professional environment, which is often very toxic.

Do you believe that the growth of the WNBA is also helping to drive research and knowledge about women's athlete health?

We are living through a moment in sports history where women have their place. And there is a commitment to women, to understanding women, to conducting research, at least here in the United States.

Many times we use male studies as a reference, and there are few studies on women, which are also of poor quality. In the last two months, the two most powerful sports research groups in the world have contacted me, because women want to know more about women and how to help women, using female parameters.

The other day you said that what is seen as an expense in Spain is an investment in the United States. From your experience, what differences would you highlight between the way the United States and Spain understand, value, and invest in sport?

Sport in Spain runs at a deficit, and that is very hard for me to understand. Here it is a business, and it is a business that is doing very well. It is a cultural issue; sport is constantly on television, men's sports, women's sports, college sports... Fans are exposed to sport for a long time.

In Spain it operates at a deficit and here it makes a huge amount of money, how can that be? What are we not doing in Spain and in Europe for it not to make as much money as it does here? The issue of sponsors and investment is different in Spain. Here you have money from ticketing, from merchandising, as well as sponsors who invest a huge amount of money.

Of course you can get better results if you invest; what people really need to rethink is how to secure resources. It’s the same sport, but in two different parts of the world.

It's not just about having technology; you also have to invest in personnel, and good people want to be paid well. It's an investment issue from top to bottom: salaries, equipment, research collaborations, advertising, marketing, etc. It's very different.

With resources and with talent, from the players, the staff, the people who make decisions, you can win. That’s the beautiful thing about the WNBA, that it’s very difficult for a team to win twice in a row; in Spain we have 3 teams that always win. It’s a complex issue.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s impact on young basketball player becomes clear when one is asked about her
articles.standfirst: Quentin Coleman had just scored 19 points for Illinois. Then he learned Caitlin Clark had been watching from the stands
articles.summary: Quentin Coleman had just scored 19 points for Illinois. Then he learned Caitlin Clark had been watching from the stands
articles.body:
Quentin Coleman had plenty to celebrate after Illinois beat Penn 112-70 on Thursday night. The freshman scored 19 points, making eight of his nine shots. But when reporters asked whether he knew Caitlin Clark was in the building, his reaction became one of the night’s most memorable moments.

Coleman’s eyes widened as he turned to teammate Zavier Zens, who had scored 18 points. “Wait, Caitlin Clark was in the building?” Coleman asked before adding, “I gotta tell my sister.” He had not realized the Indiana Fever star was sitting behind the Penn bench with her boyfriend, Connor McCaffery, the son of Penn coach Fran McCaffery.

Coleman’s biggest surprise came after the final buzzer

The surprise was genuine: Coleman and Zens said they had not known Clark was there. Coleman even joked that her presence had brought “the aura” to the arena, then connected Clark’s shooting to Zens’ own hot night from the floor.

It was an honest response, and above all, it revealed how much Caitlin Clark means to young players, even when they don’t realize the Indiana Fever star is watching their basketball skills so closely.

Caitlin Clark’s visit came during a strong start to the season for Illinois’ freshmen . Coleman was nearly perfect from the field, while Zens made four of his eight three-point attempts.

Both had already reached double figures in the team’s first two games, according to Illinois.

The scene offered a glimpse of Clark’s influence beyond the WNBA. For a young player, finding out after a big game that one of basketball’s most recognizable stars was in the stands is the kind of surprise that turns an ordinary postgame question into a story worth telling his sister.

articles.title: Brad Underwood's 'drama' with Caitlin Clark and Peja Stojakovic: "I should have done a three-point contest"
articles.standfirst: Illinois coach Brad Underwood joked that his team had been outclassed in the shooting department after two basketball icons watched the Fighting Illini dismantle Penn
articles.summary: Illinois coach Brad Underwood joked that his team had been outclassed in the shooting department after two basketball icons watched the Fighting Illini dismantle Penn
articles.body:
B rad Underwood had plenty to celebrate after Illinois produced a commanding 112–70 victory over Penn , but the coach found another talking point when he looked towards the stands.

Among the spectators were Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark and former NBA sharpshooter Peja Stojakovic , prompting Underwood to suggest that the evening needed an additional shooting competition.

There was no genuine controversy between the coach and either guest. Instead, Underwood used his postgame press conference to poke fun at his own players while acknowledging the extraordinary shooting credentials of the two visitors.

“Not only Caitlin, but Peja . I mean, we should have had a three-point contest to see who really the best shooter in the gym was,” replied Underwood , via Fighting Illini Athletics on YouTube, adding, “Because it wasn’t anybody who played tonight. No offense to any of those guys that played. But we’d probably still be out there playing a game of horse watching those two shoot.”

The joke landed particularly well because both guests had strong reasons to be at the State Farm Center on November 5. Stojakovic was watching his son Andrej represent Illinois, while Clark attended with Connor McCaffery , whose father, Fran, is the head coach of Penn.

Underwood also made a point of recognising Clark's achievements, from her college career at Iowa to her impact in the professional game. “And then what she’s done in WNBA is pretty spectacular.”

Two elite shooters with very different basketball journeys

Clark's presence offered a reminder of just how impressive her return to the court had been.

articles.title: Angel Reese’s “too small” taunt resurfaces in a pacifier jab at the Valkyries’ championship parade
articles.standfirst: A gesture that came after Atlanta took a 2-1 Finals lead resurfaced in San Francisco after Golden State won the title in seven games
articles.summary: A gesture that came after Atlanta took a 2-1 Finals lead resurfaced in San Francisco after Golden State won the title in seven games
articles.body:
Angel Reese’s “too small” gesture lasted only a moment in Game 3. But after the Golden State Valkyries beat her Atlanta Dream in the WNBA Finals, that moment followed her all the way to the champions’ parade.

Angel had reason to feel confident that night. She scored 21 points and grabbed 12 rebounds as Atlanta rolled to a 97-71 win and took a 2-1 lead in the series. During the game, she directed the gesture toward the Valkyries’ bench, including center Aminata Gueye.

The gesture returned with a championship in hand

Golden State came back to win the series in seven games, earning its first WNBA title in just its second season. At the Nov. 4 parade in San Francisco, the Game 3 taunt resurfaced in a shirt held up by former Warriors center Festus Ezeli.

It showed Reese making the gesture, with her face replaced by the crying Michael Jordan meme.

Fans also shared photos of pink pacifiers with tags showing the same meme and the words “if found, return to ATL.” The pacifiers appeared to be a fan-made joke, separate from the team’s official parade celebration.

The teasing brought the Finals rivalry into the parade, but the championship celebration was much bigger than one jab at Reese.

For Golden State, the gesture had become part of the story of a seven-game series: Atlanta had its moment, the Valkyries came back, and a taunt from Game 3 resurfaced once the title was theirs.

In the end, the Valkyries got the last laugh: they won the championship, and Reese’s “too small” taunt came back around at their parade.

articles.title: Journalist claims ESPN used Sophie Cunningham's transgender storm to fire him
articles.standfirst: Former NFL star Ryan Clark believes ESPN deliberately allowed a controversial interview with Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham to dominate the headlines as the network dealt with his departure in July
articles.summary: Former NFL star Ryan Clark believes ESPN deliberately allowed a controversial interview with Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham to dominate the headlines as the network dealt with his departure in July
articles.body:
Ryan Clark has reignited the debate surrounding his departure from ESPN, claiming the network used the controversy surrounding Sophie Cunningham 's comments on transgender athletes as a convenient distraction from the way it handled his exit.

The former NFL safety made the allegations during an appearance on the All The Smoke podcast on Thursday, November 5.

Clark suggested that the timing of Cunningham's ESPN interview, published just one day after he was informed that he was losing his job, was not coincidental.

Clark was appearing on NFL Live on July 20 when ESPN executives informed him of the decision. The following day, the network published its interview with Cunningham, whose remarks about transgender participation in women's sports quickly attracted attention well beyond the WNBA.

According to Clark , ESPN's handling of the situation helped shift the media conversation away from his dismissal. He also alleged that the network had deliberately allowed news of his departure to reach OutKick before Cunningham's interview became the major talking point.

“ Sophie Cunningham says something and they [OutKick] say, ‘A great brand switch for ESPN. Ryan Clark was fired this week and now Sophie Cunningham leads the news,'” Clark said before alleging ESPN leaked the news of his firing to OutKick.

“That’s what they [ESPN] wanted. That’s why you leaked it to them. And so I think everything points to it, but I should have — my antenna should have been up more and even with that, there was nothing I could change.”

These are Clark's allegations about ESPN's intentions, rather than an established explanation for the timing. There has been no independently confirmed evidence that the network arranged Cunningham's interview to divert attention from its personnel decisions.

Why Sophie Cunningham's comments became a major talking point

Cunningham's interview attracted considerable attention because she addressed an issue that has generated intense debate across professional women's sports.

The Indiana Fever guard told ESPN that she wanted to “protect young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men”.

Her comments prompted reactions from supporters and critics, bringing renewed attention to transgender athletes' eligibility in women's competitions.

The discussion quickly extended beyond basketball, with Cunningham receiving praise from some conservative commentators and political figures.

President Donald Trump also praised her during campaign rallies in October, according to the information surrounding the controversy.

Clark believes the resulting headlines provided ESPN with an opportunity to move the spotlight away from his departure.

However, the controversy surrounding Cunningham's remarks was independently significant, and there is no confirmed evidence that she was involved in any decision concerning Clark's employment.

The former Pittsburgh Steelers safety also suggested that he had noticed warning signs in the months before he was dismissed.

He pointed to his absence from promotional material connected to ESPN's coverage of Super Bowl 2027, despite having been a prominent member of its NFL programming.

“There was a commercial first and when they did the commercial Marcus [Spears] and Laura [Rutledge] were in it … I’m not involved,” Clark said.

“But most of the people that are on ‘Monday Night Countdown’ were a part of it. But I had gotten so used to being treated a certain way and not put on the front that I wasn’t even tripping about it.

“Then we went to Fanatics Fest [in July] and Disney had something that was posted about the Super Bowl [in 2027] and I wasn’t on it. So I say all that to say, that this was the plan.”

Clark joined ESPN in 2015 following his NFL playing career and became one of the network's recognisable football analysts. He also received a Sports Emmy in May 2023 for Outstanding Personality/Studio Analyst.

His departure attracted considerable attention because of the unusual circumstances. ESPN reportedly accelerated its notification after receiving media inquiries about his position, with executives concerned that news of the decision would become public before they could inform him directly.

He consequently learned about the move while appearing on NFL Live and did not return to finish the programme.

This is not the first time Clark has questioned the way ESPN handled his exit. During an appearance on The Breakfast Club in October, he described the decision as “purposeful” and accused the network of intentionally leaking the news to “humiliate” him.

Clark has since begun building his career outside the broadcaster. His podcast, The Pivot, which he hosts alongside former NFL players Fred Taylor and Channing Crowder, secured a multi-year partnership with Netflix in August.

He has also launched a weekly live NFL studio programme with NFL Studios.

Nevertheless, his professional options remain affected by his ESPN contract. Clark explained that a non-compete arrangement prevents him from working as an NFL analyst for another network until the agreement expires at the end of February.

His latest comments suggest that the circumstances of his departure remain a source of frustration.

While Cunningham's interview became a major sports-media story, Clark believes the timing helped ESPN avoid sustained attention over the way it handled his dismissal. Whether the two events were deliberately connected, however, remains unproven.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd confirm their breakup
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Wings teammates have revealed that their romantic relationship ended more than a year ago
articles.summary: The Dallas Wings teammates have revealed that their romantic relationship ended more than a year ago
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd have finally addressed the questions surrounding their relationship, confirming that they are no longer a couple despite continuing to share the court as teammates with the Dallas Wings .

The announcement came during the latest episode of Fudd's podcast, Fudd Around and Find Out, where the two basketball stars explained that their separation happened considerably earlier than many fans had assumed.

Fudd introduced the subject herself, making it clear that they wanted to put an end to the uncertainty rather than allow speculation to continue.

“ Paige and I have something that we want to share with everyone,” Fudd said on the podcast. “We are no longer together.

Bueckers then clarified that the breakup had actually happened more than a year ago, meaning the pair were already separated before Dallas selected Fudd with the first overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft.

“We were not together before she got drafted. So all of those narratives can go to bed,” Bueckers said.

That clarification is particularly significant because their personal connection had become a talking point when the Wings reunited the former UConn teammates in Dallas.

Questions had emerged about whether their relationship played any part in the organisation's decision to select Fudd , but Bueckers firmly rejected that suggestion.

“She was not drafted because she was my girlfriend. She was drafted because she deserved it. She’s an amazing human, amazing basketball player,” she said.

The announcement also explained how the pair managed to navigate an entire professional season together despite no longer being romantically involved.

Rather than allowing their private circumstances to affect their work, they insist that their friendship and commitment to basketball have remained intact.

From UConn champions to teammates in Dallas

Bueckers and Fudd have known each other since their teenage years, first meeting through USA Basketball before eventually becoming teammates at the University of Connecticut.

Their connection grew during their college careers, and they played important roles in helping the Huskies capture the 2025 NCAA national championship.

Bueckers was selected first overall by Dallas in the 2025 WNBA Draft, while Fudd followed the same path a year later. The Wings made Fudd the No. 1 pick in April 2026, bringing the former college teammates together again.

Their relationship had attracted considerable attention after Bueckers publicly acknowledged it in 2025 during an appearance on the WAG Talk TikTok show.

The pair had previously kept much of their personal lives private, making their eventual confirmation a significant moment for supporters.

When questions about their relationship surfaced during Dallas' media day in April, Bueckers had already made clear that she wanted to keep her private life separate from her professional responsibilities.

The team's media staff had also declined to discuss the players' personal circumstances during Fudd's introductory press conference.

Now, Bueckers has explained that there was no romantic relationship to complicate their reunion as teammates.

“We’re still friends. We’re still cool. We played an entire season together,” she continued. “We’re the utmost professionals. We care about basketball.

“Sometimes in life, there are just seasons. And sometimes in life, two people are just at different points in their lives,” Bueckers added. “We still support each other. We’re still going to be great friends. We’re still going to be great teammates.”

The pair also addressed the negative reaction and intrusive messages that have surrounded speculation about their private lives, asking supporters not to direct hostility towards their friends and families. They made it clear that the announcement was intended to settle the matter, rather than invite further scrutiny.

Their basketball careers will continue to bring them together in Dallas, where Bueckers has established herself as one of the franchise's leading players and Fudd has begun her own WNBA journey.

Fudd's rookie campaign included an average of 13.1 points per game before a knee injury brought her season to an early end, while Bueckers continued to develop after winning Rookie of the Year in 2025.

Ultimately, the message from both players was that their relationship has changed, but their mutual respect has not.

Bueckers and Fudd have confirmed the breakup, yet they appear determined to ensure that it does not define their professional partnership or overshadow what they hope to achieve together on the basketball court.

articles.title: Angel Reese pulls off a ‘Michael Jackson’ move after WNBA defeat and return to LSU
articles.standfirst: Fresh off of a WNBA Finals loss, Reese took some time out to go back to her roots.
articles.summary: Fresh off of a WNBA Finals loss, Reese took some time out to go back to her roots.
articles.body:
When looking at the big picture, Angel Reese 's first season with the Atlanta Dream was just that, a dream come true. Leaving a Chicago Sky franchise that didn't value her enough, Reese helped lead the Dream to the WNBA Finals .

Reese and the Dream came six points away from winning it all, but ultimately fell short to an elite Golden State Valkyries team. Reese oozed positivity despite the crushing loss following the game, choosing to highlight the way her teammates and the Dream franchise has treated her so far.

Angel Reese returned to LSU and was honored by her alma mater

With her heart full thanks to her Dream teammates, Reese decided to keep the good vibes going this week, as she returned to her roots at LSU . The Tigers honored Reese with a crown and a bouquet of roses during halftime of their game against Texas Southern, giving her a proper send-off following an outstanding WNBA season.

Reese was, per usual, dressed to the nines. Her black and white outfit featured one detail that reminded some of Michael Jackson , surprisingly. Her white gloves weren't exactly the same form factor as MJ's iconic accessory, but it was still a show-stopping outfit as a whole.

Reese spent two seasons at LSU following two seasons at Maryland. With the Tigers, she won the National Championship in 2023 and was an All-American in both seasons.

articles.title: The Nike Caitlin 1 “Friendship Bracelet” sneakers leave Jimmy Fallon in shock when he checks out their amazing details
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever superstar brought a special pair of her Taylor Swift-inspired signature sneakers to The Tonight Show
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever superstar brought a special pair of her Taylor Swift-inspired signature sneakers to The Tonight Show
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark managed to steal the spotlight on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon for reasons beyond her basketball achievements, as her latest Nike sneakers left the presenter struggling to hide his excitement.

During her appearance on Friday, November 6, the Indiana Fever guard introduced Fallon to the Nike Caitlin 1 “Friendship Bracelet” colourway, a design inspired by Taylor Swift and the colourful bracelets exchanged by fans during the pop superstar's Eras Tour.

Clark arrived with a surprise for the host: a personalised pair of the unreleased shoes. Fallon immediately appreciated the gesture when he realised that the sneakers had been made especially for him.

“Dude, I'm freaking out right now,” he exclaimed as he examined the gift.

The pair featured an additional detail that made them different from the version expected to reach the public. The words “Tonight Show” appeared on the personalised design, giving Fallon a unique edition of Clark's signature basketball shoe.

“Look at those,” Fallon said, before admiring the customisation and asking about the charms attached to the laces.

Clark explained that the design would allow buyers to add their own personality to the sneakers. The colorful charms can be used to customize the appearance, giving fans an opportunity to make their pairs feel more individual rather than simply purchasing an identical shoe off the shelf.

The host was so impressed that he immediately wanted to put them on, with Clark happily giving him permission.

Taylor Swift's influence is all over Clark's latest Nike design

The inspiration behind the Friendship Bracelet colorway is closely connected to Clark's admiration for Swift . The singer's Eras Tour helped popularize the tradition of fans making and trading colorful bracelets, often featuring song titles, initials and personal messages.

Clark has experienced that tradition herself, regularly receiving bracelets from supporters when signing autographs. During the interview, she explained why bringing the idea into her sneaker collection felt like a natural move.

“Yeah, obviously I'm a big Taylor fan and— Me too,” Clark said when Fallon brought up Swift.

She also discussed the connection between the bracelets and her supporters, explaining that the footwear was intended to give something back to the people who have embraced her: “And I think a lot of my games, like, people always bring Friendship Bracelets. They want to trade. So I was like, ‘Let's put it on a shoe. How fun. People can make it their own’."

Clark also revealed that Swift had already seen the design and approved of it: “Taylor likes them, yeah.”

The sneakers have several details that make the connection unmistakable. Their pearl-like upper features shifting pastel shades, while fuzzy laces carry colourful beads spelling out “CC” and “22”, representing Clark's initials and jersey number.

The insole also continues the bracelet theme with decorative graphics surrounding her signature double-C logo.

The release is currently expected in February 2027, meaning fans will have to wait before getting their hands on the pair. Clark told Fallon she expected them to arrive towards the end of that month.

The friendship-bracelet design is not the only example of Clark using her signature collection to express her interests.

In recent weeks, she has showcased several different Caitlin 1 versions, including the Halloween-themed “Jinx” edition, a Chiefs -inspired red-and-gold design and other distinctive colourways such as “Berry Fade” and “Cave Stone”.

Her connection with Swift also extends beyond the sneakers. The two have spent time together at Kansas City Chiefs games, including watching the team from a VIP suite at Arrowhead Stadium.

Clark was invited into the high-profile setting through Travis Kelce , Swift's husband, and the friendship has helped make the singer's influence on her footwear an especially personal touch.

Clark's appearance on Fallon's programme came during a busy week away from the basketball court. Alongside discussing her Nike collection, she was promoting her children's book, EXTRAordinary! articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has built her reputation on making seemingly impossible shots look routine. But the Indiana Fever superstar found a completely different way to showcase her shooting touch during an appearance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. Clark became the star of an unexpected cheeseball challenge with the NBC host , turning a ridiculous late-night game into an entertaining display of accuracy, excitement and competitive spirit.

The challenge was simple: Clark had 24 seconds to shoot as many cheeseballs as possible into Fallon’s mouth from approximately six feet away. What followed was a hilarious sequence that quickly brought out the competitive side of the WNBA star. Fallon caught the first seven shots, and Clark became increasingly animated as the cheeseballs continued finding their target

“COME ON!” she shouted during the challenge, celebrating each successful attempt as though she were knocking down another three-pointer in a playoff game.

A very different kind of spotlight

By the time the clock expired, the pair had managed to complete an impressive 12 successful catches in 24 seconds. Clark raised her hand and pumped her fist in celebration before exchanging a high-five with Fallon , who was still trying to speak with his mouth full.

“Oh my god! That was the best shooter in the world!” Fallon exclaimed. Clark could hardly contain her excitement, responding with a simple but fitting reaction: “That was amazing!” The WNBA’s official account on X also joined the fun, sharing the clip with the caption: “This is amazing.”

The cheeseball challenge offered a very different kind of spotlight for a player accustomed to performing in front of thousands of basketball fans, and another reminder of why Clark has become one of the most recognizable personalities in American sports.

Clark’s late-night appearance comes during a busy Offseason

Clark’s appearance on Fallon’s show also provided a glimpse into how she is spending her time away from the basketball court. The Fever star was promoting her new children’s book and latest signature shoe release, adding another stop to an increasingly busy offseason that has included appearances outside the WNBA.

Last month, Clark appeared on College GameDay in Iowa and also attended a Kansas City Chiefs game alongside Taylor Swift. Her appearance on Fallon’s program offered another opportunity to showcase her personality beyond basketball.

Clark’s second professional season ended in the WNBA Playoffs , where Indiana lost its first-round series 2-1 to the Las Vegas Aces . However, after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign, she has reasons to approach this offseason differently.

Rather than concentrating primarily on recovering from physical setbacks, the former Iowa star wants to use the coming months to improve her game and build strength ahead of her fourth WNBA season. During her recent exit interview, Clark explained that reviewing her performances will be an important part of that process.

She also acknowledged that her priorities have changed compared with last offseason, when getting healthy while continuing to develop her basketball skills was a major challenge.

articles.title: Angel Reese's request to Shaquille O'Neal ends badly: the copied gesture from Shaq that angered the Atlanta Dream star
articles.standfirst: The NBA legend could not resist mocking Reese with her own signature celebration during an appearance together at LSU
articles.summary: The NBA legend could not resist mocking Reese with her own signature celebration during an appearance together at LSU
articles.body:
Angel Reese thought she was giving Shaquille O'Neal an opportunity to say something on camera. Instead, the former NBA champion used the moment to turn the tables on the Atlanta Dream star by copying one of her most recognizable celebrations.

The incident happened on the sidelines at Tiger Stadium before LSU's football team faced Alabama on Saturday.

Reese , who played college basketball for the Tigers , was spending time with O'Neal , another famous LSU alumnus, when she pointed her camera towards him and asked him to say something.

Rather than delivering a message, the four-time NBA champion brought his thumb and index finger together to perform the "too small" gesture that has become closely associated with Reese .

The reaction was immediate. Reese could be heard responding, "it's okay, it's okay," before playfully pushing her camera towards O'Neal as though she were taking a shot at him.

The exchange appeared lighthearted, but it was another reminder that Reese has struggled to escape the consequences of using the celebration during the WNBA Finals. Even someone she considers a mentor has now joined in the teasing.

O'Neal's involvement is particularly interesting because the pair share a close relationship that goes beyond their connection to LSU .

Reese has previously described the basketball legend as a father figure, making the exchange look more like friendly banter than a serious disagreement.

How Reese's own celebration became a running joke

The gesture originally attracted widespread attention during Game 3 of the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries .

Atlanta had taken control of the contest, eventually winning 97-71 to move ahead 2-1 in the series. With less than 30 seconds remaining, Reese directed the "too small" motion towards Golden State's bench, seemingly suggesting that the Valkyries were not physically capable of stopping her.

However, the series took a very different direction after that result.

Golden State recovered to win the next two games before Atlanta forced a deciding seventh contest. The Valkyries ultimately secured the championship with a 68-63 victory on October 31.

Gabby Williams was the standout performer, scoring 30 points, including 28 in the second half, to earn Finals MVP honors. Reese finished the deciding game with eight points and 12 rebounds.

The celebrations afterwards brought more attention to Reese's earlier taunt. Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg copied the gesture while celebrating the championship, while former Golden State center Festus Ezeli took the joke further during the team's November 4 parade.

Ezeli displayed a shirt showing Reese performing the celebration, with her face replaced by the famous crying Michael Jordan meme. He subsequently wore the shirt and mimicked the gesture himself.

O'Neal has now added his name to that growing list.

Why Shaq and Reese share such a close bond

The teasing is unlikely to change the relationship between the two basketball figures.

O'Neal played at LSU between 1989 and 1992, becoming one of the university's most celebrated athletes before embarking on his Hall of Fame NBA career.

Reese also spent two seasons with the Tigers, winning the 2023 NCAA national championship before being selected seventh overall by the Chicago Sky in the 2024 WNBA Draft.

Their connection became especially visible in March 2024, when O'Neal joined Reese's mother to escort her onto the court for LSU Senior Day.

Reese has previously explained how much his support means to her, describing him as someone who has stood beside her through difficult periods and cares about her as a person rather than simply as an athlete.

That makes the latest exchange a particularly amusing moment. O'Neal clearly knows exactly which button to press, and Reese's playful response suggests she understood the joke.

Still, with the Finals defeat and subsequent celebrations keeping the "too small" gesture alive, the Atlanta star may have to accept that opponents, former players and even her closest basketball mentor are not going to let her forget it anytime soon.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's new plans face a conflict with basketball as she awaits news about her future
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard has renewed her ambition to appear on Dancing with the Stars, but the show's schedule and uncertainty surrounding her WNBA contract could complicate her next move
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard has renewed her ambition to appear on Dancing with the Stars, but the show's schedule and uncertainty surrounding her WNBA contract could complicate her next move
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has made no secret of her interest in exploring opportunities beyond basketball, and a recent visit to the set of Dancing with the Stars appears to have strengthened that ambition.

The Indiana Fever guard has now spoken again about wanting to compete on the popular ABC program, although fitting the experience around her professional commitments remains a significant obstacle.

Cunningham discussed the possibility during an episode of her podcast, No Hesitation, which she co-hosts with basketball development coach Drew Hanlen .

The 30-year-old explained that she has maintained contact with the show's representatives over the past couple of years, but the timing has repeatedly made participation difficult.

“I truly do hope that I can do it one day,” Cunningham said. “It gets in the way of our WNBA season. So, that’s kind of my hold-up, but it’s not out of the question.”

Her comments came after she attended a live recording of the competition and met professional dancer Daniella Karagach . The encounter was particularly memorable because Karagach recognized Cunningham and encouraged her to consider joining the cast.

“She is so beautiful and just a great [expletive] dancer,” the Fever player said. “And she saw me, she was like, ‘Oh my gosh, I’m a huge fan,’ and I was like, ‘I’m a huge fan of you.’

“And she goes, ‘Well, come next season … come be my partner next year. You can lift me up.’ And I was like, ‘Oh. That’s awesome.‘ So it was so cool. It was a really fun experience.”

The invitation was an exciting moment for Cunningham , although it does not mean that she has officially secured a place on a future season. Her interest is clear, but the calendar presents a problem.

Cunningham's basketball future remains unsettled

Dancing with the Stars traditionally begins its fall season in September, precisely when the WNBA is approaching the end of its regular-season schedule and preparing for the playoffs.

For a player hoping to remain part of a competitive team, committing to several weeks of rehearsals and live performances could be difficult.

There is another reason Cunningham's immediate future is attracting attention. Her one-year contract with Indiana covered the 2026 campaign, meaning she is now an unrestricted free agent and can consider opportunities elsewhere.

Cunningham returned to the Fever in April after recovering from a right knee MCL tear that ended her 2025 season.

She had previously joined Indiana from the Phoenix Mercury ahead of the 2025 campaign and became a popular presence through her physical approach, outside shooting and energetic personality.

Her 2026 regular-season contribution included 7.9 points per game across 43 appearances, while she shot 41.9% from three-point range.

Those numbers give interested teams a clear picture of her value as an experienced perimeter player. However, Indiana has several roster decisions to make before the next season.

General manager Amber Cox praised Cunningham's influence when discussing the team's free agents, describing her as a strong locker-room leader who brings experience and personality. Cox also made clear that the organization wanted to have conversations about her future, without guaranteeing a new agreement.

That leaves Cunningham facing two separate questions: where she will play in 2027 and whether she can eventually find a way to pursue television opportunities without sacrificing her basketball career.

For now, neither a return to Indiana nor a place on Dancing with the Stars has been confirmed. Her enthusiasm for the show is unmistakable, but the next stage of her professional career may determine when that ambition can become reality.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark offers support to her boyfriend Connor McCaffery after his brother's difficult situation: "Cancer sucks"
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star joined a wave of support for the McCaffery family after Connor revealed that his younger brother Jack had been diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star joined a wave of support for the McCaffery family after Connor revealed that his younger brother Jack had been diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has shown her support for boyfriend Connor McCaffery following heartbreaking news about his younger brother, Jack.

The University of Richmond basketball player has been diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma, prompting an emotional response from his family and an outpouring of encouragement from across the basketball world.

Connor shared the news through an Instagram post featuring photographs of himself and Jack growing up together.

Alongside the childhood memories, he made clear that his younger brother would not have to face the difficult period ahead without the people closest to him: “Nobody stronger than u to fight this. You’ve got us all with you, and we love you. CANCER SUCKS!!!!!!!!”

Clark was among those responding to the post, leaving a row of red heart emojis to show her support. The Fever guard was joined by teammates and other familiar names from the Indiana basketball community, including Lexie Hull and Kelsey Mitchell .

Another particularly heartfelt message came from Jade Haliburton, the wife of Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton . She addressed Connor directly, writing: “Praying for Jack and your whole family, Connor! He’s got a whole crew behind him!!!!”

The messages reflect how closely connected the basketball community in Indiana has become.

Connor previously played for the Iowa Hawkeyes and now works as a player development assistant with the Noblesville Boom, the Pacers' G League affiliate. Clark, meanwhile, is one of the leading figures in the WNBA with the Indiana Fever .

Jack McCaffery begins treatment after Richmond diagnosis

Richmond announced on November 8 that Jack, a sophomore forward, had been diagnosed with Hodgkin’s lymphoma and would take an indefinite medical leave from the men's basketball program.

The university explained that its medical staff had evaluated him earlier in the week. Following that assessment, Jack traveled home with his parents to Philadelphia and was admitted to the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, where he has begun treatment under the supervision of Penn Medicine specialists.

His father, Fran McCaffery , who coaches the Penn men's basketball team, expressed gratitude to the people who helped arrange his son's care.

“We are grateful to the Richmond coaching staff and medical team for their prompt response, and to Kevin Mahoney and the doctors and nurses here at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. He is in great hands, and our family feels blessed to be here, where Jack’s care is directed by this world-class care team,” Fran said.

There was also an encouraging assessment from Dr. Alison Wakoff Loren of Penn Medicine, who is overseeing the treatment plan: “Any cancer diagnosis is distressing, especially at a young age, but we are confident in Jack’s treatment plan and Penn Medicine’s team of lymphoma experts. Hodgkin’s lymphoma mainly affects young people in their 20s, but it is a highly curable form of cancer, thanks to years of dedicated research. Our goal is to get Jack through his treatments safely and to return him to school and to his teammates on the basketball court as soon as we can.”

A difficult experience the family has faced before

The diagnosis is especially painful for the McCaffery family because it is not their first experience with cancer. Jack's older brother Patrick was diagnosed with thyroid cancer in 2014, when he was just 14 years old.

Patrick underwent treatment and eventually returned to basketball, going on to play at the college level.

His experience has brought another layer of concern to the family's latest challenge, although Jack's diagnosis is different and his treatment will be determined by his medical team.

Jack's basketball journey has already included some difficult interruptions. He played his freshman season at Butler in 2025-26 before transferring to Richmond.

He appeared in nine games for the Bulldogs, averaging 2.8 points and 1.6 rebounds, according to reports. His immediate priority is now his health rather than his return to the court.

Richmond coach Chris Mooney also praised Jack's character and importance to the program, promising that the team would stand behind him and his family throughout his recovery.

For Connor , Clark and everyone who has reached out, the focus is firmly on supporting Jack through treatment.

The encouraging words from Penn Medicine offer hope, while the response from friends, teammates and the wider basketball community demonstrates just how many people are standing with the McCaffery family.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal’s blunt response after going viral for mocking Angel Reese with “too small” celebration
articles.standfirst: A playful encounter between the two basketball stars attracted attention online
articles.summary: A playful encounter between the two basketball stars attracted attention online
articles.body:
Shaquille O'Neal has responded to speculation about his relationship with Angel Reese after a lighthearted encounter between the two LSU basketball legends became an unexpected social media controversy.

The former Los Angeles Lakers superstar attracted attention during Saturday's LSU football game against Alabama when he recreated the "too small" gesture that Reese had directed toward an opponent during the WNBA Finals.

Footage showed Reese approaching O'Neal with her phone and encouraging him to address the camera, only for the four-time NBA champion to respond with the familiar hand signal.

Reese appeared surprised by the gesture and playfully moved her hand toward O'Neal as he laughed and walked away, prompting some viewers to interpret her reaction as genuine frustration.

However, O'Neal subsequently addressed the attention on Instagram, posting a photograph of himself performing the same celebration alongside Reese .

"Don't believe everything you see on the internet, people," he wrote.

The brief response appeared to challenge the suggestion that the exchange had caused tension between the pair, although O'Neal didn't explain precisely which claims he was disputing.

The celebration became a major talking point during Game 3 of the 2026 WNBA Finals, when Reese helped the Atlanta Dream defeat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71.

Reese produced 21 points and 12 rebounds before directing the gesture toward Golden State's bench, apparently targeting center Aminata Gueye after their exchanges throughout the series.

Atlanta's victory established a 2-1 series advantage, leaving the Dream within two wins of capturing the championship.

However, Golden State recovered from that deficit and eventually secured the title with a 68-63 victory in Game 7 on October 31.

Reese finished the deciding contest with eight points and 12 rebounds, and her earlier celebration subsequently became a target for rival players and supporters.

During Golden State's championship festivities, members of the organization and fans repeatedly referenced the gesture, including at the team's November 4 parade.

That history made O'Neal 's decision to recreate it particularly noticeable, especially because Reese had already faced criticism following Atlanta's defeat.

Shaq and Angel Reese's close relationship

Despite the attention surrounding Saturday's exchange, O'Neal and Reese have maintained a supportive relationship since meeting through their shared connection to LSU.

O'Neal starred for the Tigers between 1989 and 1992, while Reese helped the women's basketball program capture its first national championship in 2023.

The former NBA center has supported Reese 's professional development, including helping establish her relationship with Reebok before she entered the WNBA.

He also joined Reese 's mother during her Senior Day celebrations in 2024, reflecting a personal connection that extends beyond basketball.

Reese has previously described O'Neal as a father figure, making suggestions of a serious disagreement difficult to establish from the brief video alone.

Saturday's reunion came during LSU's 31-13 defeat against Alabama, with both basketball stars among several prominent guests invited to the game.

O'Neal 's subsequent Instagram response suggests he wanted viewers to reconsider the encounter rather than assume the gesture reflected genuine hostility.

articles.summary: The WNBA star continues to attract attention away from the basketball court, and her latest social media moment has fans hooked
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has a way of making headlines even when she is nowhere near a basketball court, and she has done it again . The WNBA star is no stranger to stealing the spotlight, but this time, it was her dance moves that caught everyone's attention.

Her popularity has continued to grow, and while she remains one of the league's most controversial personalities, fans are increasingly interested in what she does outside basketball and how she spends her free time.

Since joining the Indiana Fever, Cunningham has built considerable momentum on social media , becoming one of the most followed players in the league. According to a report by The Sporting News , her Instagram growth has surpassed the combined gains of 49 other WNBA stars.

A different side of Sophie Cunningham

Her outspoken opinions have divided fans, but social media has given people another reason to follow her . Away from the debates surrounding her basketball career, Cunningham regularly shares a more playful side of her personality, and a recent video featuring her dancing in a brown dress was no exception. Her Shakira-like moves quickly caught viewers' attention, leaving many hooked on the performance.

The numbers have also drawn attention because Cunningham reportedly now has more Instagram followers than her Fever teammate Caitlin Clark , one of the biggest names in women's basketball. One possible reason is their different approaches to social media, with Cunningham maintaining a much more active presence while Clark tends to be more reserved , particularly during the offseason.

Her life beyond the basketball court

Cunningham regularly keeps her followers updated through dance videos, family moment s, time with her animals and activities that have little to do with basketball. That constant connection has helped her build an audience interested in more than just her performances on the court .

Whatever comes next in her basketball career, Cunningham has already developed a following that extends well beyond the Indiana Fever fan base, and moments like her latest dance continue to keep her in the spotlight.

articles.body:
WNBA star Angel Reese went viral after an amusing courtside interaction with a man who tried to flirt with her but repeatedly got her name wrong.

The incident occurred on Friday, November 6, 2026, during the New Orleans Pelicans' game against the Minnesota Timberwolves at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans.

Reese was sitting courtside in a striking zebra-print outfit when a man seated behind her began complimenting her appearance.

He addressed her as "Angela Reece" instead of Angel Reese.

The basketball star turned around, thanked him for the compliment and corrected her name.

The man immediately acknowledged his mistake, explaining that tequila had played a role in his confusion.

Rather than ending the conversation, he continued complimenting Reese, including a playful reference to her zebra-print clothing.

The interaction was recorded and shared on social media, where the man's mistaken attempt at flirting attracted attention.

Reese was attending the game to support her younger brother, Julian Reese, who plays for the New Orleans Pelicans on a two-way NBA contract.

The Pelicans officially acknowledged her presence on social media, celebrating the reunion of the basketball siblings.

Julian did not play that night, and New Orleans lost to Minnesota 115-109 in an NBA Cup matchup.

articles.body:
Angel Reese attended the game between the New Orleans Pelicans and the Minnesota Timberwolves to support her younger brother. During the game, a fan began recording her from the stands and called her "Angela Reese". The basketball player decided to correct him with a brief response: "Thanks, but my name is Angel".

The man apologized and blamed his mistake on the tequila he had been drinking. Afterwards, he continued with the compliments toward the player , who was wearing a zebra-print outfit. "You're the sexiest zebra I've seen here," he told her. Reese responded with an "Okay" and a smile.

The exchange was captured in a video posted on Instagram by a New Orleans comedian, and later drew the attention of users.

Angel's presence also reflects the relationship the two have maintained since their early years in basketball. The brothers were together at the University of Maryland during the 2021-22 season and shared a team before continuing their respective careers.

Throughout their careers, both have acknowledged the influence of their mother, Angel Webb Reese, on their athletic development.

Angel Reese's mother played college basketball at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC), and later pursued a professional career abroad, playing in European leagues (such as in Luxembourg). After separating from her husband, she raised her children Angel and Julian Reese as a single mother, passing on her sporting legacy to them.

This time, the Las Vegas star was in the stands to support Julian, although she ended up drawing some of the attention because of an unexpected encounter with a fan who got her name wrong when addressing her, and Angel, true to her style, made it clear what her name is.

The interview took an unexpected turn when Cowherd hesitantly described Cunningham as a sex symbol of the WNBA, prompting an amused reaction from the basketball star. The clip resurfaced on social media in November.

Cunningham laughed and explained that she had expected Cowherd to use a much less flattering description. The host then elaborated on what he considered an interesting contrast: Cunningham's aggressive, fearless attitude on the court and her confidence in expressing her femininity through fashion and glamorous pregame outfits.

Cunningham embraced that combination, explaining that she has always loved dressing up, wearing heels and expressing her feminine side. She challenged the idea that female basketball players must choose between looking glamorous and competing with toughness and intensity.

The interview coincided with the launch of Cunningham's revamped podcast, No Hesitation, distributed through Cowherd's media company, The Volume. The exchange attracted mixed reactions online, with some fans enjoying her humor while others questioned Cowherd's choice of words.
