articles.title: Juju Watkins doesn't allow anyone to make disparaging comments about Caitlin Clark: “Don't do that”
articles.standfirst: The USC superstar refused to join an announcer's attempt to diminish Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: The USC superstar refused to join an announcer's attempt to diminish Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
J uju Watkins had just delivered one of the most remarkable individual performances in women's college basketball , but she was not interested in using the occasion to put another superstar down.

After scoring 51 points against Stanford in February 2024, the USC guard was asked about her achievement in an interview that quickly took an unexpected turn when Caitlin Clark 's name entered the conversation.

Watkins had every reason to enjoy the spotlight. Her performance helped the Trojans secure a 67-58 victory over Stanford, setting a new USC single-game scoring record and establishing the highest individual total in Division I women's basketball that season.

She also collected 11 rebounds, four steals and six three-pointers.

The interviewer initially highlighted the scale of her accomplishment, pointing out that nobody else in the country had scored more points in a single game that season. However, the conversation took a different direction when he jokingly asked: “There's a lot of players in the country playing Division 1 basketball. Nobody scored more points in one game this year than you. That's the most. Caitlin Clark who?”

Rather than accepting the comparison or playing along with the apparent dig, Watkins immediately interrupted the suggestion: “No, no, no. Don't do that. Don't do that. Don't do that. Much respect, Eric.”

Her response was delivered with a smile, but the message was unmistakable. Watkins wanted recognition for her own achievement without having to dismiss another player to make it seem more impressive.

The moment quickly attracted attention from basketball fans, many of whom praised the young star for refusing to turn a historic night into an opportunity to disrespect Clark .

Watkins and Clark have both helped transform women's basketball

The exchange was particularly interesting because Clark and Watkins represent two generations of talent who have helped attract greater attention to women's basketball.

Clark became one of the sport's biggest attractions during her time at Iowa, where her extraordinary shooting range, scoring ability and playmaking helped bring new audiences to the women's college game.

She eventually became the NCAA Division I all-time leading scorer in women's basketball before entering the WNBA in 2024.

Watkins , meanwhile, established herself as one of the most exciting young players in the country at USC.

Her 51-point performance against Stanford was not simply a memorable individual display; it demonstrated why she was already being discussed as a potential future professional superstar.

The two players have occasionally been placed in the same conversation because of their scoring ability and influence on the sport. However, Watkins ' reaction showed that she did not believe one player's success needed to come at the expense of another.

That attitude has remained relevant as women's basketball continues to attract unprecedented attention. Comparisons between stars can generate headlines, but they can also distract from the achievements taking place on the court.

Watkins has made an impressive comeback from injury

Watkins ' story has since included another major challenge. She missed the entire 2025-26 college season after suffering a torn ACL during the 2025 NCAA Tournament, spending an extended period recovering before returning to action in November 2026.

Her comeback has already produced encouraging results. She scored 21 points in USC's season-opening victory over UNLV before delivering 32 points, 16 rebounds, six assists and five steals in a 118-40 win against Utah State on November 8.

The senior guard is once again establishing herself as one of college basketball's leading players, having previously averaged 23.9 points per game during the 2024-25 season. USC has also named her its preseason Big Ten Player of the Year.

Importantly, the famous 51-point performance against Stanford happened in February 2024, not during her current 2026-27 comeback season. It remains one of the defining moments of her young career.

Her response to the announcer is another reason that performance continues to be remembered.

Watkins could have embraced the comparison and allowed the exchange to become a debate about who was better. Instead, she chose to acknowledge Clark's achievements.

For a player whose own career is attracting enormous expectations, it was a simple but powerful demonstration of respect. Watkins wanted her 51 points to speak for themselves, without needing to diminish somebody else's accomplishments.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham’s ‘sex symbol’ moment with Colin Cowherd wasn’t what she expected
articles.standfirst: The WNBA guard was caught off guard when the conversation took an unexpected turn
articles.summary: The WNBA guard was caught off guard when the conversation took an unexpected turn
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has become one of the WNBA's most controversial figures, both for her views and her personality on the court. She has openly supported the position that transgender women should not compete in women's sports, while her competitive approach has also led to confrontations with other players. Her willingness to defend her team, physical style of play and tendency to get under opponents' skin have made her a polarizing figure in the league.

That may explain why Cunningham was caught off guard during her interview with Colin Cowherd. As the host tried to address how people in the WNBA perceive her, he appeared unsure about how to introduce the subject . Cunningham may have expected the conversation to move toward some of the criticism surrounding her opinions and behavior, but the direction it took was different.

An unexpected description

Being described as a sex symbol was clearly not what Cunningham anticipated. She even seemed to take the label as a compliment, helping ease the awkwardness of the exchange. Cowherd also appeared to recognize that the term could be considered outdated and controversial in today's media environment, but Cunningham's reaction made the moment less uncomfortable.

Still, labels like this tend to open larger discussions on social media. The debate is not necessarily about whether someone should feel complimented, but about whether calling a woman a sex symbol reduces her identity to her physical appearance and sexual appeal. Others, meanwhile, s ee it as a traditional expression of widespread popularity and attractiveness in pop culture.

The debate over how women athletes are portrayed

For Cunningham, who has expressed more traditional views on several subjects, the description may have been easier to accept than it would be for other athletes who want their sporting achievements to take priority over their appearance . The concern is that these labels can contribute to the continued sexualization of public figures, particularly women, in the media.

The discussion also connects to the criticism surrounding Sydney Sweeney's controversial advertising campaign, which reignited conversations about how women's bodies are used to attract attention. Female athletes already face the challenge of being treated as objects of public interest rather than as complete individuals , with the male gaze and the entertainment industry's standards of desirability often shaping how they are presented.

Not everyone applauded Cunningham's reaction to Cowherd's description. S ome argued that accepting t he label oversimplifies a complex career and personality , making it seem as though women are valued primarily for their looks rather than their talent and work. However, Cunningham's personal response also deserves to be respected. If she chose to take the description as a compliment, that does not mean everyone else has to share her interpretation, even as the broader debate about how women in sports are portrayed continues.
